blocks.text: Tsawwassen Farms: what the ground is and what governs it

items.t: Hobby acreage or working farm: to keep BC Assessment farm status, a property must keep meeting the minimum farm income, which goes up with the size of the farm, and that affects its value.

Typical buyer (characterization, not a sourced statistic): working farmers in the Delta belt, hobby-farm and horse buyers on the smaller acreages, and buyers who want ALR land within reach of Tsawwassen and Ladner services.

Municipality and plan: City of Delta. Tsawwassen is one of Delta's three communities (Ladner, Tsawwassen and North Delta), planned under the Delta Official Community Plan (Bylaw No. 8400, 2024), a single plan that replaced the former area plans. Its agriculture policies apply to Delta's farmland.
Treaty-land boundary: Tsawwassen First Nation Lands sit on Tsawwassen's western edge. TFN land follows TFN law, not City bylaws.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect acreage buyers

parts.t: The rules that apply across Delta (zoning, suites, strata, land and taxes) are on one page:
buying a home in Delta: the rules

items.t: Subdividing farmland: in Delta's A1 zone, subdivision is allowed only if it fits the Official Community Plan and is approved by the Agricultural Land Commission where the ALR applies, with an 8 ha minimum for new lots (except a home-site severance under the Commission's policy). A2 also has an 8 ha minimum, and A3 doesn't allow subdivision.

Water: wells and aquifers are listed in the provincial well database; well reports must be filed within 90 days of a well being built, changed or closed, and older wells may not be listed. Domestic groundwater use doesn't need a licence, but other uses, including irrigation, need a water licence.

The edge of Tsawwassen has two sets of rules: a drive toward Ladner crosses Delta properties designated Agriculture (A) under the Official Community Plan, and where a property is in the ALR, the Agricultural Land Commission's housing, subdivision and no-strata rules apply on top. Check a specific property on the Commission's map to see which rules apply; the area name won't tell you.

Farm ditches trigger an urban-sounding permit area: Every Delta property within 30 m of a stream, slough or ditch — including a working farm's drainage ditch — falls in the Streamside Protection and Enhancement Development Permit Area, so a setback check that buyers associate with city lots applies in the middle of working farm land.

The current OCP, Bylaw No. 8400 (2024), designates farm land "Agriculture (A)". City reports and listings that predate July 2024 may refer to the earlier area plans; read them against the current OCP.

Sellers: gather what a farm buyer asks for first. That means the farm income history that supports the farm classification, and any water licences or Agricultural Land Commission approvals in place. A farm buyer's lender and lawyer will ask for those first, and having them ready keeps a sale from stalling.

faq.a: On ALR land, one additional residence is permitted without an ALC application where the conditions are met — 90 m² or less on parcels of 40 ha or smaller, 186 m² or less on larger parcels — and Delta bylaws must also permit it; the A1 zone allows one accessory farm dwelling unit within those same size limits, and a secondary suite is permitted only inside the principal residence.
faq.q: Can a Tsawwassen-area farm have a second dwelling?

faq.a: Check the water; don't assume it: search the provincial well database (GWELLS) for the well record (older wells may not appear). If the farm irrigates, confirm its water licence. Using groundwater for anything other than household use, including irrigation, needs a licence under the Water Sustainability Act; household use doesn't.
faq.q: Can I irrigate, and what should I check about water?

faq.a: Southlands-side parcels can sit in hazard DPA SD3 (2.9 m floor level, 2.3 m minimum land surface elevation, 7.5 m tidal setback), and any lot within 30 m of a ditch or slough is in the Streamside Protection and Enhancement DPA — farm ditches count. Confirm both with the City, not from a listing's wording.
faq.q: What do the dike and ditch rules mean for a Southlands-side parcel?

faq.a: Both. Delta's Official Community Plan (Bylaw No. 8400, 2024) designates farmland on the edges of Tsawwassen "Agriculture (A)", and Agricultural Land Reserve rules apply where land is in the ALR. The urban neighbourhoods are residential; the farms are on that agricultural edge and in the farmland toward Ladner.
faq.q: Is there real farmland in Tsawwassen, or is it all residential?
